title: Aegis Release Broker — adaptive traffic brokerage, shadow probing, and auto-rollback policy engine
creator: Priya Nair
description: Build an extensible policy engine (Aegis Release Broker) that brokers user traffic between model variants, runs controlled shadow probes, evaluates safety and quality gates in near-real time, and triggers automated rollback or mitigation actions. Must support declarative policy descriptions, per-customer overrides, multi-metric guardrails (latency, error-rate, quality regressions), and both ratio-based and rule-based splits. This ticket covers the core orchestration, runtime hooks for metric evaluation, and a lightweight auditing trail for compliance reviews.
acceptance_criteria: Policy DSL implemented with support for step schedules, time-based holds, and shadow probes
Runtime broker can route traffic by percentage and by query-surface rules (e.g., user_tier, region, route)
Metric evaluation pipeline emits per-step pass/fail decisions within 10s of metric window completion
Automatic rollback action triggers on configurable composite guardrail breaches and records an auditable revert event
Per-customer override feature respects RBAC and logs access for KMS/HSM-backed customers
End-to-end integration test covering routing, shadowing, guardrail breach, and rollback scenarios
design_decisions: Use a small, embeddable policy evaluator (Lua-like sandbox) to keep policy evaluation close to routing layer for low latency
Keep policy DSL declarative and composable; avoid Turing-complete constructs to simplify verification and audits
Metrics evaluated at a sliding window granularity (30s default) with exponential backoff on unstable signals to prevent flip-flop
Shadow probes run with configurable sampling ratios and never affect production quotas or billing; results feed into offline quality dashboards and live guardrails
Rollback actions are two-phased: immediate traffic reversion + follow-up remediation issue creation in Linear with attachments
engineering_notes: Prototype broker as a sidecar routing service for canary experiments to minimize blast radius
Integrate with existing tracing hooks in Redwood Console to tag traffic by policy_id and step_id
Cache policy evaluations per-request fingerprint for 60s to reduce evaluation QPS at the router
Fallback behavior: if policy service is unavailable, default to safe variant defined in policy (usually baseline model)
We need to add a backend metrics topic (kafka) for guardrail signals; will reuse the existing telemetry schema but add guardrail_type and policy_id fields
tradeoffs_and_risks: Pros of embedded evaluation: lower latency, simpler observability; Cons: more complexity in router and harder to hot-reload policies without rollout
Using short sliding windows improves detection speed but increases false positives during traffic spikes
Shadow probing provides signal for quality regressions but adds additional infrastructure costs and complexity for correlating results to production errors
Two-phased rollback reduces flapping but may delay remediation for severe incidents; mitigation: emergency immediate-cut override path for SREs
implementation_plan: Week 1-2: Policy DSL spec, wireframe of policy editor in Console, and proto for policy JSON schema
Week 3-4: Implement router-side policy evaluator and sidecar prototype; add tagging to requests
Week 5: Integrate guardrail metric emission and subscription; build composite guardrail evaluator service
Week 6: Hook automated rollback action to deployment controller and create Linear issue template for revert triage
Week 7: E2E tests, load tests, and initial private-beta with 2 customers
Week 8: Collect feedback, harden, and prepare for runtime-1.22 cut
test_plan: Unit tests for DSL parser and policy evaluator (edge cases for percent math and rule precedence)
Integration tests simulating gradual traffic increase with injected metric regressions to verify rollback timing
Chaos tests where policy service is killed to validate fallback behavior
Shadow probe correlation tests to ensure we can attribute quality regressions to a variant with >95% confidence
Performance tests to ensure policy evals add <5ms p95 to routing latency
rollout_plan: Internal dogfood rollout to staging agents with synthetic traffic and realtime dashboards
Private beta: enable for two enterprise customers under a feature flag; collect SLO/guardrail telemetry
Gradual enablement of auto-rollback: start with alert-only mode for first two weeks, then enable auto-revert with human-in-loop
Public rollout after 4 weeks of stable beta signals and sign-off from Compliance and SRE
open_questions: Should policy definitions live in Console only, or be importable via API (we favor both; need auth model)?
What is the canonical metric store for composite guardrails when customers use external APMs?
Do we surface rollback rationale to end customers via webhooks, or only to account admins?
How to model gradual degradation (e.g., slow quality drift) vs. abrupt failures in guardrail logic?
